title: Preventing Water Seal Loss in P-Traps
description: A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, self-siphonage can strip this water seal if the trap arm drops vertically before reaching a vent—effectively creating an unvented S-trap configuration. To maintain a stable water seal, ensure the trap arm runs horizontally to a proper vent connection before turning downward. Proper venting balances atmospheric pressure within the drain system, preventing negative pressure from pulling the liquid seal out of the trap during discharge.

Preventing Water Seal Loss in P-Traps

A P-trap relies on a standing water seal to block sewer gases from entering living spaces. However, self-siphonage can strip this water seal if the trap arm drops vertically before reaching a vent—effectively creating an unvented S-trap configuration. To maintain a stable water seal, ensure the trap arm runs horizontally to a proper vent connection before turning downward. Proper venting balances atmospheric pressure within the drain system, preventing negative pressure from pulling the liquid seal out of the trap during discharge.
